analysis: This batch contains only documentation and static-asset changes, with no executable code, no authentication, attestation, encryption or billing changes, and no runtime configuration. Files: changelog.d/landing-community-headlines.md (a new 4-line changelog fragment about landing page headlines and horizontal story browsing); docs/assets/landing-community/hero.jpg and stories.jpg (new binary images, no text content to inspect); docs/developer/build.md (a 2-line addition at about line 984 noting that landing test dependencies include jsdom for DOM-based story gesture regressions, installed by `npm ci`). I checked the added docs text against the threat model. It touches no trust boundary (TB-001 through TB-011), asset or threat. jsdom is described as a dev/test dependency of the landing marketing app, which sits outside the coordinator and provider trust boundaries. The patch does not show landing/package.json or lockfile changes, so a later pass should confirm any jsdom addition is a devDependency, is pinned or lockfile-covered, and does not enter the production build. I did not see that code here, so there is a coverage limit rather than evidence of risk. Binary images were not content-inspected, but they live under docs/assets and are not served by the coordinator. No cross-file interactions needing integration attention.
